title: Tokamak or stellarator?
description: Why a magnetic fusion machine needs twisted field lines, how the tokamak twists them with a plasma current and the stellarator with three-dimensional coils, the toroidal field of ITER's coils, pulsed and steady operation, and the limitations of each design.

sources.title: Tokamak (Wikipedia): Tamm and Sakharov, toroidal and poloidal fields, drifts in a purely toroidal field, plasma current and the transformer, disruptions
Stellarator (Wikipedia): Spitzer 1951, no induced plasma current, an inherently steady-state machine
Wendelstein 7-X (Wikipedia): 50 non-planar and 20 planar superconducting coils, first plasma 10 December 2015, 8-minute plasma in February 2023
CEA: WEST record of 1337 s on 12 February 2025 with lower hybrid current drive
WEST (formerly Tore Supra) (Wikipedia): Tore Supra's 6 min 30 s plasma in December 2003; WEST 22 min 17 s in 2025
Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (Wikipedia): 1056 s on 30 December 2021, 1066 s on 20 January 2025
US ITER: toroidal field coil conductor fact sheet (18 coils, 134 turns, 68 kA, 5.3 T)
ITER Organization: magnets (central solenoid drives 15 MA for 300 to 500 s; peak toroidal field 11.8 T)
CIEMAT fusion wiki: ITER reference scenario (R = 6.2 m, a = 2.0 m, 15 MA, 5.3 T)
